FICTIONAL TEST REPORT
CT BRAIN WITHOUT CONTRAST
Date of examination: 03/02/2025
Clinical details: Sudden onset headache, 58 year old, no focal neurology.
Technique: Axial 5 mm contiguous slices from skull base to vertex without intravenous contrast.
FINDINGS:
There is no acute intracranial haemorrhage. The grey-white matter differentiation is preserved. No extra-axial collection is seen. The ventricular system is normal in size and configuration, with the fourth ventricle midline. A small area of low attenuation measuring 8 mm is seen in the left periventricular white matter, in keeping with chronic small vessel change. The basal cisterns are patent. No midline shift. The visualised paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are clear. The calvarium is intact.
IMPRESSION:
1. No acute intracranial haemorrhage or large territorial infarct.
2. Mild chronic small vessel ischaemic change, left periventricular white matter.
